operations.old: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. (a) Let $G$ be a connected nilpotent affine algebraic group over $k$; then $Z(G)_s$, the largest subgroup of the centre of multiplicative type, is the largest algebraic subgroup of $G$ of multiplicative type ([[def-group-of-multiplicative-type-and-torus]]), it is central and characteristic, and $G/Z(G)_s$ is unipotent ([[def-unipotent-algebraic-group]]); if $G$ is smooth then $Z(G)_s$ is a torus, and over a perfect field the smooth connected nilpotent groups are exactly the products $U\times T$ with $U$ unipotent and $T$ a torus. (b) For a smooth connected affine group variety $G$ and a torus $S\subseteq G$, the torus $S$ is maximal among the tori of $G$ if and only if $C_G(S)/S$ contains no nontrivial torus.
